extracted.intended_audience: prospective grantees, nonprofit organizations, and the general public interested in Hewlett Foundation funding
extracted.subtask_description: A listing of the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation's program areas and high-level funding priorities describing what kinds of projects and goals the foundation supports. Useful for potential applicants to determine alignment with grantmaking interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall approach to grantmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The William and Flora Hewlett Foundation began in 1966 with the broad purpose of promoting the well-being of humanity. We make grants across a number of program areas, many of which we have supported for decades. Our grantmaking also addresses emerging challenges through time-limited initiatives. To understand what we fund and why, learn more about our programs and initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the foundation funds both long-running program areas and time-limited initiatives; applicants should consider whether their work aligns with sustained programs or emerging, time-limited opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education
rubrics_metrics.description: The Education Program makes grants that provide students with rigorous, relevant, and innovative educational opportunities, including open educational resources and practices, in order to foster mobility and help students contribute to the future of their communities and our country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority areas include rigor, relevance, innovation, and support for open educational resources/practices; projects improving student mobility and community contribution are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Philanthropy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Effective Philanthropy Program seeks to strengthen the capacity of Hewlett Foundation grantees, and nonprofits and philanthropy in general, to benefit people, communities, and the planet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants focus on strengthening organizational capacity and the effectiveness of the philanthropic sector broadly; proposals should demonstrate capacity-building or field-strengthening impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Environment Program makes grants to address climate change globally and to conserve the U.S. West to ensure people, communities, and the planet flourish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual priorities: global climate-change work and conservation of the U.S. West; applicants should align with one of these geographic/scientific emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender Equity and Governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gender Equity and Governance Program seeks to foster inclusive societies where everyone can thrive. Focusing on East and West Africa, Mexico, and the U.S., the program makes grants to expand women’s access to reproductive health and economic opportunity; increase governments’ responsiveness to the people they serve; and improve policymaking through the effective use of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program defines geographic focus (East & West Africa, Mexico, U.S.) and thematic priorities: reproductive health, economic opportunity for women, government responsiveness, and evidence-based policymaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performing Arts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Performing Arts Program makes grants to support meaningful artistic experiences for communities throughout the San Francisco Bay Area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographically focused on the San Francisco Bay Area and emphasizes community-centered artistic experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Democracy Program makes grants to strengthen our shared national community through nonpartisan support for our governing institutions in an effort to build public trust in a durable democracy where all Americans have a meaningful opportunity to thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonpartisan support for governing institutions and activities that build public trust and inclusive civic opportunity are priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and Society
rubrics_metrics.description: The Economy and Society Initiative works to identify and help spread ideas from across the ideological spectrum about what’s next for capitalism in order to meet the challenges of the 21st century so all people thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on idea-generation and dissemination across ideological perspectives about future directions for capitalism; projects that surface or scale policy/idea solutions are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racial Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Racial Justice Initiative promotes equal opportunity for all by addressing systemic inequalities across issue areas and in society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is work that confronts systemic inequalities across multiple issue areas to promote equal opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Projects responds to opportunities that advance our philanthropic values, incubate new ideas, strengthen our field, and support the Bay Area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for opportunistic, exploratory, or field-building work that aligns with foundation values or regional support for the Bay Area; typically time-limited or experimental.
